sanskrit: śaknoti jīvituṃ dakṣo nālasaḥ sukham edhate dṛśyante jīvaloke 'smin dakṣāḥ prāyo hitaiṣiṇaḥ
english: The capable man is able to live; the slothful man does not prosper in ease. Here in the world of the living it is the capable, for the most part, who are seen to be the friends of their own welfare.

sanskrit: yadi dakṣaḥ samārambhāt karmaṇāṃ nāśnute phalam nāsya vācyaṃ bhavet kiṃ cit tattvaṃ cāpy adhigacchati
english: If a capable man, for all his undertaking of deeds, does not reap their fruit, no blame whatever can fall upon him, and he yet arrives at the truth of things.

sanskrit: akṛtvā karma yo loke phalaṃ vindati viṣṭitaḥ sa tu vaktavyatāṃ yāti dveṣyo bhavati prāyaśaḥ
english: But he who in the world wins a reward without having done the work, sitting idle, makes himself liable to censure and for the most part becomes an object of hatred.

sanskrit: evam etad anādṛtya vartate yas tv ato 'nyathā sa karoty ātmano 'narthān naiṣa buddhimatāṃ nayaḥ
english: He who, disregarding this truth, conducts himself otherwise brings ruin upon himself; this is not the way of the wise.

sanskrit: hīnaṃ puruṣakāreṇa yadā daivena vā punaḥ kāraṇābhyām athaitābhyām utthānam aphalaṃ bhavet hīnaṃ puruṣakāreṇa karma tv iha na sidhyati
english: When effort is wanting in human exertion, or again in destiny, or in both these causes together, then endeavor proves fruitless; and a deed that lacks human exertion does not succeed here.

sanskrit: daivatebhyo namaskṛtya yas tv arthān samyag īhate dakṣo dākṣiṇyasaṃpanno na sa moghaṃ vihanyate
english: But he who, having paid homage to the gods, rightly strives after his aims—capable and endowed with skill—is not struck down in vain.

sanskrit: samyag īhā punar iyaṃ yo vṛddhān upasevate āpṛcchati ca yac chreyaḥ karoti ca hitaṃ vacaḥ
english: And this, again, is right striving: that a man attends upon his elders, asks them what is best, and acts upon their salutary counsel.

sanskrit: utthāyotthāya hi sadā praṣṭavyā vṛddhasaṃmatāḥ te 'sya yoge paraṃ mūlaṃ tanmūlā siddhir ucyate
english: Rising up again and again, one should always question those honored by the aged; they are the supreme root of his enterprise, and success is said to be rooted in them.

sanskrit: vṛddhānāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā yo hy utthānaṃ prayojayet utthānasya phalaṃ samyak tadā sa labhate 'cirāt
english: He who, having heard the word of the elders, then applies himself to exertion, soon obtains in full measure the fruit of that exertion.

sanskrit: rāgāt krodhād bhayāl lobhād yo 'rthān īheta mānavaḥ anīśaś cāvamānī ca sa śīghraṃ bhraśyate śriyaḥ
english: The man who strives after his ends out of passion, anger, fear, or greed—without self-mastery and full of arrogance—swiftly falls away from prosperity.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ duryodhanenārtho lubdhenādīrghadarśinā asamarthya samārabdho mūḍhatvād avicintitaḥ
english: This very aim was begun by Duryodhana—greedy, short-sighted—without due preparation, undertaken in folly and without reflection.

sanskrit: hitabuddhīn anādṛtya saṃmantryāsādhubhiḥ saha vāryamāṇo 'karod vairaṃ pāṇḍavair guṇavattaraiḥ
english: Disregarding those of benevolent counsel, taking counsel instead with the wicked, and though dissuaded, he wrought enmity with the Pāṇḍavas, who were the worthier in virtue.

sanskrit: pūrvam apy atiduḥśīlo na dainyaṃ kartum arhati tapaty arthe vipanne hi mitrāṇām akṛtaṃ vacaḥ
english: Of exceedingly evil character even before, he ought not now to give way to despair; for when an undertaking has come to ruin, it is the unheeded word of friends that scorches the heart.

sanskrit: anvāvartāmahi vayaṃ yat tu taṃ pāpapūruṣam asmān apy anayas tasmāt prāpto 'yaṃ dāruṇo mahān
english: But because we followed in the train of that wicked man, this great and terrible calamity has now come upon us as well.

sanskrit: anena tu mamādyāpi vyasanenopatāpitā buddhiś cintayataḥ kiṃ cit svaṃ śreyo nāvabudhyate
english: And my mind, even now tormented by this disaster, though it ponders, cannot in any way discern what is for its own good.

sanskrit: muhyatā tu manuṣyeṇa praṣṭavyāḥ suhṛdo budhāḥ te ca pṛṣṭā yathā brūyus tat kartavyaṃ tathā bhavet
english: A man bewildered should question his wise and well-wishing friends; and whatever they, being asked, may say, that should be done accordingly.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca gāndhārīṃ ca sametya ha upapṛcchāmahe gatvā viduraṃ ca mahāmatim
english: Let us, then, go and approach Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Gāndhārī, and the great-minded Vidura too, and inquire of them.

sanskrit: te pṛṣṭāś ca vadeyur yac chreyo naḥ samanantaram tad asmābhiḥ punaḥ kāryam iti me naiṣṭhikī matiḥ
english: And whatever they, being asked, may declare to be best for us in the time at hand, that we should thereupon do—such is my settled conviction.

sanskrit: anārambhāt tu kāryāṇāṃ nārthaḥ saṃpadyate kva cit kṛte puruṣakāre ca yeṣāṃ kāryaṃ na sidhyati daivenopahatās te tu nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
english: From the non-undertaking of tasks no end is ever accomplished; and those whose task does not succeed though human exertion has been made are stricken down by destiny—about them there need be no debate.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca kṛpasya vacanaṃ śrutvā dharmārthasahitaṃ śubham aśvatthāmā mahārāja duḥkhaśokasamanvitaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Having heard the auspicious words of Kṛpa, joined with righteousness and reason, Aśvatthāman, O great king, was filled with grief and sorrow.

sanskrit: dahyamānas tu śokena pradīptenāgninā yathā krūraṃ manas tataḥ kṛtvā tāv ubhau pratyabhāṣata
english: Burning with grief as though by blazing fire, he then hardened his mind to cruelty and addressed those two in reply.

sanskrit: puruṣe puruṣe buddhiḥ sā sā bhavati śobhanā tuṣyanti ca pṛthak sarve prajñayā te svayā svayā
english: In each and every man his own particular understanding seems fair to him, and all alike take satisfaction, each in his own wisdom.

sanskrit: sarvo hi manyate loka ātmānaṃ buddhimattaram sarvasyātmā bahumataḥ sarvātmānaṃ praśaṃsati
english: For every man in the world deems himself the wiser; to each his own self is held in high regard, and each man praises his own self.

sanskrit: sarvasya hi svakā prajñā sādhuvāde pratiṣṭhitā parabuddhiṃ ca nindanti svāṃ praśaṃsanti cāsakṛt
english: For every man's own wisdom is fixed in self-approval; men blame another's understanding and praise their own again and again.

sanskrit: kāraṇāntarayogena yoge yeṣāṃ samā matiḥ te 'nyonyena ca tuṣyanti bahu manyanti cāsakṛt
english: Those whose judgment, through the play of differing causes, happens to agree in an undertaking take satisfaction in one another and esteem each other highly, again and again.

sanskrit: tasyaiva tu manuṣyasya sā sā buddhis tadā tadā kālayogaviparyāsaṃ prāpyānyonyaṃ vipadyate
english: Yet in one and the same man this or that understanding, from time to time, undergoes a reversal as circumstances change, and one judgment falls out of accord with another.

sanskrit: acintyatvād dhi cittānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ cittavaikalyam āsādya sā sā buddhiḥ prajāyate
english: For because the minds of men are unfathomable, and especially so, it is upon coming into some derangement of mind that this or that understanding is born in them.

sanskrit: yathā hi vaidyaḥ kuśalo jñātvā vyādhiṃ yathāvidhi bheṣajaṃ kurute yogāt praśamārtham ihābhibho
english: Just as a skilled physician, having duly diagnosed a disease, prepares a remedy by sound method for the sake of its cure, O lord—

sanskrit: evaṃ kāryasya yogārthaṃ buddhiṃ kurvanti mānavāḥ prajñayā hi svayā yuktās tāṃ ca nindanti mānavāḥ
english: so do men form a judgment for the accomplishment of a task; yet though endowed with their own wisdom, men afterward find fault with that very judgment.

sanskrit: anyayā yauvane martyo buddhyā bhavati mohitaḥ madhye 'nyayā jarāyāṃ tu so 'nyāṃ rocayate matim
english: In youth a mortal is beguiled by one cast of mind, in middle life by another, and in old age he comes to favor yet another judgment.

sanskrit: vyasanaṃ vā punar ghoraṃ samṛddhiṃ vāpi tādṛśīm avāpya puruṣo bhoja kurute buddhivaikṛtam
english: And again, upon meeting with terrible adversity, or with prosperity of like measure, a man, O Bhoja, undergoes a transformation of his understanding.

sanskrit: ekasminn eva puruṣe sā sā buddhis tadā tadā bhavaty anityaprajñatvāt sā tasyaiva na rocate
english: In one and the same man this or that understanding arises from time to time, and because his wisdom is impermanent, that very judgment ceases to please him.

sanskrit: niścitya tu yathāprajñaṃ yāṃ matiṃ sādhu paśyati tasyāṃ prakurute bhāvaṃ sā tasyodyogakārikā
english: But the resolve which, having decided according to his wisdom, a man sees to be sound—upon that he fixes his intent, and it becomes the spur to his exertion.

sanskrit: sarvo hi puruṣo bhoja sādhv etad iti niścitaḥ kartum ārabhate prīto maraṇādiṣu karmasu
english: For every man, O Bhoja, once he has resolved "this is right," sets about gladly to perform it, even in deeds that lead to death and the like.

sanskrit: sarve hi yuktiṃ vijñāya prajñāṃ cāpi svakāṃ narāḥ ceṣṭante vividhāś ceṣṭā hitam ity eva jānate
english: For all men, having grasped a course of action and their own wisdom too, exert themselves in manifold endeavors, deeming each one to be for their good.

sanskrit: upajātā vyasanajā yeyam adya matir mama yuvayos tāṃ pravakṣyāmi mama śokavināśinīm
english: This resolve of mine that has arisen today, born of calamity, I shall declare to you both—a resolve that is the destroyer of my grief.

sanskrit: prajāpatiḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā karma tāsu vidhāya ca varṇe varṇe samādhatta ekaikaṃ guṇavattaram
english: The Lord of Creatures, having created beings and ordained their tasks, established in each several class one special excellence above the rest.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇe damam avyagraṃ kṣatriye teja uttamam dākṣyaṃ vaiśye ca śūdre ca sarvavarṇānukūlatām
english: In the Brāhmaṇa, unwavering self-restraint; in the Kṣatriya, the highest valor; in the Vaiśya, skill; and in the Śūdra, willing service to all the classes.

sanskrit: adānto brāhmaṇo 'sādhur nistejāḥ kṣatriyo 'dhamaḥ adakṣo nindyate vaiśyaḥ śūdraś ca pratikūlavān
english: An unrestrained Brāhmaṇa is no true man; a Kṣatriya without valor is base; a Vaiśya is blamed if he lacks skill, and a Śūdra if he is contrary.

sanskrit: so 'smi jātaḥ kule śreṣṭhe brāhmaṇānāṃ supūjite mandabhāgyatayāsmy etaṃ kṣatradharmam anu ṣṭhitaḥ
english: I am born in the most excellent and honored lineage of Brāhmaṇas; yet through ill fortune I have taken up this duty of the Kṣatriya.

sanskrit: kṣatradharmaṃ viditvāhaṃ yadi brāhmaṇy asaṃśritam prakuryāṃ sumahat karma na me tat sādhu saṃmatam
english: If, while knowing the Kṣatriya's duty, I were to perform some very great deed grounded instead in the Brāhmaṇa's way, that would not be thought becoming in me.

sanskrit: dhārayitvā dhanur divyaṃ divyāny astrāṇi cāhave pitaraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā kiṃ nu vakṣyāmi saṃsadi
english: Having borne the celestial bow and celestial weapons in battle, yet having seen my father slain, what shall I say in the assembly of men?

sanskrit: so 'ham adya yathākāmaṃ kṣatradharmam upāsya tam gantāsmi padavīṃ rājñaḥ pituś cāpi mahādyuteḥ
english: Therefore today, embracing that Kṣatriya's duty according to my will, I shall go upon the path of the king, and of my father too, of mighty splendor.

sanskrit: adya svapsyanti pāñcālā viśvastā jitakāśinaḥ vimuktayugyakavacā harṣeṇa ca samanvitāḥ vayaṃ jitā matāś caiṣāṃ śrāntā vyāyam anena ca
english: This night the Pāñcālas will sleep, trusting and wearing the look of victors, their yokes and armor cast off and filled with joy, holding that we are beaten and worn out by our exertion.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ niśi prasuptānāṃ svasthānāṃ śibire svake avaskandaṃ kariṣyāmi śibirasyādya duṣkaram
english: Upon them, as they sleep at ease in the night within their own camp, I shall this day make a hard onslaught upon the encampment.

sanskrit: tān avaskandya śibire pretabhūtān vicetasaḥ sūdayiṣyāmi vikramya maghavān iva dānavān
english: Falling upon them in the camp, senseless and as good as corpses, I shall strike them down by my valor, as Maghavat struck down the Dānavas.

sanskrit: adya tān sahitān sarvān dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamān sūdayiṣyāmi vikramya kakṣaṃ dīpta ivānalaḥ nihatya caiva pāñcālāñ śāntiṃ labdhāsmi sattama
english: This day I shall strike down by my valor all of them gathered together, led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, as a blazing fire consumes dry grass; and having slain the Pāñcālas, I shall win peace, O best of men.

sanskrit: pāñcāleṣu cariṣyāmi sūdayann adya saṃyuge pinākapāṇiḥ saṃkruddhaḥ svayaṃ rudraḥ paśuṣv iva
english: I shall range among the Pāñcālas this day, slaying them in battle, as Rudra himself, the Pināka in hand, in fury ranges among the beasts.

sanskrit: adyāhaṃ sarvapāñcālān nihatya ca nikṛtya ca ardayiṣyāmi saṃkruddho raṇe pāṇḍusutāṃs tathā
english: This day, having slain and cut down all the Pāñcālas, I shall in my fury crush in battle the sons of Pāṇḍu as well.

sanskrit: adyāhaṃ sarvapāñcālaiḥ kṛtvā bhūmiṃ śarīriṇīm prahṛtyaikaikaśas tebhyo bhaviṣyāmy anṛṇaḥ pituḥ
english: This day, having strewn the earth with the bodies of all the Pāñcālas, smiting them down one by one, I shall become free of my debt to my father.

sanskrit: duryodhanasya karṇasya bhīṣmasaindhavayor api gamayiṣyāmi pāñcālān padavīm adya durgamām
english: This day I shall send the Pāñcālas upon that hard road traveled by Duryodhana, by Karṇa, by Bhīṣma, and by the lord of the Saindhavas as well.

sanskrit: adya pāñcālarājasya dhṛṣṭadyumnasya vai niśi virātre pramathiṣyāmi paśor iva śiro balāt
english: This day, in the dead of night, I shall by main force crush the head of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the king of the Pāñcālas, as one crushes the head of a sacrificial beast.

sanskrit: adya pāñcālapāṇḍūnāṃ śayitān ātmajān niśi khaḍgena niśitenājau pramathiṣyāmi gautama
english: This day, in the night, I shall crush in combat with my whetted sword the sleeping sons of the Pāñcālas and the Pāṇḍavas, O Gautama.

sanskrit: adya pāñcālasenāṃ tāṃ nihatya niśi sauptike kṛtakṛtyaḥ sukhī caiva bhaviṣyāmi mahāmate
english: This day, having slain that host of the Pāñcālas in their sleep by night, I shall be a man whose purpose is fulfilled and who is content, O great-minded one.

sanskrit: kṛpa uvāca diṣṭyā te pratikartavye matir jāteyam acyuta na tvā vārayituṃ śakto vajrapāṇir api svayam
english: Kṛpa said: By good fortune this resolve to requite the foe has arisen in you, O undecaying one; not even the wielder of the thunderbolt himself were able to turn you back.

sanskrit: anuyāsyāvahe tvāṃ tu prabhāte sahitāv ubhau adya rātrau viśramasva vimuktakavacadhvajaḥ
english: But we two together shall follow you at dawn; tonight take your rest, your armor and banner laid aside.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tvām anuyāsyāmi kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ parān abhimukhaṃ yāntaṃ rathāv āsthāya daṃśitau
english: I shall follow you, and Kṛtavarman of the Sātvatas as well, both mounting our chariots and clad in mail, as you advance to face the enemy.

sanskrit: āvābhyāṃ sahitaḥ śatrūñ śvo 'si hantā samāgame vikramya rathināṃ śreṣṭha pāñcālān sapadānugān
english: United with us two, tomorrow in the encounter you shall slay the foe, displaying your valor, O best of chariot-warriors—the Pāñcālas together with their followers.

sanskrit: śaktas tvam asi vikrāntuṃ viśramasva niśām imām ciraṃ te jāgratas tāta svapa tāvan niśām imām
english: You are well able to display your valor; rest this night. Long have you kept awake, dear son; sleep, then, for this one night.

sanskrit: viśrāntaś ca vinidraś ca svasthacittaś ca mānada sametya samare śatrūn vadhiṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ
english: Rested, your sleep taken, and your mind at ease, O bestower of honor, you shall meet the foe in battle and slay them—of that there is no doubt.

sanskrit: na hi tvā rathināṃ śreṣṭha pragṛhītavarāyudham jetum utsahate kaś cid api deveṣu pāvakiḥ
english: For when you, O best of chariot-warriors, son of the Fire, have taken up your choicest weapons, none even among the gods has the power to conquer you.

sanskrit: kṛpeṇa sahitaṃ yāntaṃ yuktaṃ ca kṛtavarmaṇā ko drauṇiṃ yudhi saṃrabdhaṃ yodhayed api devarāṭ
english: As the son of Droṇa advances, joined with Kṛpa and arrayed beside Kṛtavarman, who—even the king of the gods—could do battle with him, raging in the fight?

sanskrit: te vayaṃ pariviśrāntā vinidrā vigatajvarāḥ prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ vai nihaniṣyāma śātravān
english: We, well rested, our sleep taken, and our fever of grief gone, will slay our enemies when the night has given way to dawn.

sanskrit: tava hy astrāṇi divyāni mama caiva na saṃśayaḥ sātvato 'pi maheṣvāso nityaṃ yuddheṣu kovidaḥ
english: For yours are celestial weapons, and mine too, beyond doubt; and the Sātvata also is a mighty archer, ever skilled in battles.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ sahitās tāta sarvāñ śatrūn samāgatān prasahya samare hatvā prītiṃ prāpsyāma puṣkalām viśramasva tvam avyagraḥ svapa cemāṃ niśāṃ sukham
english: We three together, dear son, having by main force slain in battle all the foes assembled, shall win abundant joy. Rest, then, untroubled, and sleep this night in comfort.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca kṛtavarmā ca prayāntaṃ tvāṃ narottama anuyāsyāva sahitau dhanvinau paratāpinau rathinaṃ tvarayā yāntaṃ rathāv āsthāya daṃśitau
english: I and Kṛtavarman, both bowmen and scorchers of the foe, mounting our chariots and clad in mail, shall together follow you, O best of men, as you set forth—a chariot-warrior advancing in haste.

sanskrit: sa gatvā śibiraṃ teṣāṃ nāma viśrāvya cāhave tataḥ kartāsi śatrūṇāṃ yudhyatāṃ kadanaṃ mahat
english: Having gone to their camp and proclaimed your name aloud in the battle, you shall then work great slaughter among the enemies as they fight.

sanskrit: kṛtvā ca kadanaṃ teṣāṃ prabhāte vimale 'hani viharasva yathā śakraḥ sūdayitvā mahāsurān
english: And when you have wrought their slaughter, you shall in the clear light of dawn disport yourself as Śakra did when he had struck down the great Asuras.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi śakto raṇe jetuṃ pāñcālānāṃ varūthinīm daityasenām iva kruddhaḥ sarvadānavasūdanaḥ
english: For you are able to conquer in battle the host of the Pāñcālas, as the slayer of all the Dānavas, in his wrath, conquered the army of the Daityas.

sanskrit: mayā tvāṃ sahitaṃ saṃkhye guptaṃ ca kṛtavarmaṇā na saheta vibhuḥ sākṣād vajrapāṇir api svayam
english: When you are joined with me in the fray and guarded by Kṛtavarman, not even the mighty wielder of the thunderbolt himself, in person, could withstand you.

sanskrit: na cāhaṃ samare tāta kṛtavarmā tathaiva ca anirjitya raṇe pāṇḍūn vyapayāsyāva karhi cit
english: And neither I in battle, dear son, nor Kṛtavarman likewise, will ever withdraw from the fight until we have conquered the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: hatvā ca samare kṣudrān pāñcālān pāṇḍubhiḥ saha nivartiṣyāmahe sarve hatā vā svargagā vayam
english: Having slain in battle the base Pāñcālas together with the Pāṇḍavas, we shall all return—or else, slain, we shall go to heaven.

sanskrit: sarvopāyaiḥ sahāyās te prabhāte vayam eva hi satyam etan mahābāho prabravīmi tavānagha
english: At dawn we ourselves shall be your helpers by every means; this I declare to you truly, O mighty-armed and sinless one.

sanskrit: evam uktas tato drauṇir mātulena hitaṃ vacaḥ abravīn mātulaṃ rājan krodhād udvṛtya locane
english: Thus addressed in salutary words by his maternal uncle, the son of Droṇa then answered his uncle, O king, his eyes rolling with wrath.

sanskrit: āturasya kuto nidrā narasyāmarṣitasya ca arthāṃś cintayataś cāpi kāmayānasya vā punaḥ
english: Whence comes sleep to a man who is anguished, and who is consumed with rage, who broods over his purposes, or who again is filled with longing?

sanskrit: tad idaṃ samanuprāptaṃ paśya me 'dya catuṣṭayam yasya bhāgaś caturtho me svapnam ahnāya nāśayet
english: See how all four of these have come upon me today; any one quarter of them would in a moment destroy my sleep.

sanskrit: kiṃ nāma duḥkhaṃ loke 'smin pitur vadham anusmaran hṛdayaṃ nirdahan me 'dya rātryahāni na śāmyati
english: What grief in this world can equal the remembrance of my father's slaying? It burns my heart, and today, by night and by day, it gives me no rest.

sanskrit: yathā ca nihataḥ pāpaiḥ pitā mama viśeṣataḥ pratyakṣam api te sarvaṃ tan me marmāṇi kṛntati
english: And the manner in which my father, above all, was slain by those wicked men—you yourself witnessed it all—that cuts me to the very vitals.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi mādṛśo loke muhūrtam api jīvati droṇo hateti yad vācaḥ pāñcālānāṃ śṛṇomy aham
english: How indeed can one like me live in this world even for a moment, when I hear the words of the Pāñcālas: "Droṇa is slain"?

sanskrit: dṛṣṭadyumnam ahatvājau nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe sa me pitṛvadhād vadhyaḥ pāñcālā ye ca saṃgatāḥ
english: Without slaying Dhṛṣṭadyumna in battle I have no wish to live; he, for the murder of my father, must die, and so must the Pāñcālas who were leagued with him.
